summary: Canvas-tool umbrella over MPI-379 / 421 / 382 / 368 / 375 / 373 - six cards on one surface (MpiCanvasViewer plus the MPI-381 MpiMaskStrip rail), each one changing what the next is built on. Opened straight in doing because its first step starts now. That step is a BRAINSTORM WITH THE USER on MPI-379, not implementation: the user's position 2026-08-01 is that the real feature is A LOT SIMPLER than the card, which carries three rounds of parked options - a second detection engine (COCO YOLO plus an R2 upload and the segm-vs-bbox folder trap), a per-pixel index map, an unsettled box-vs-blob hover affordance, and a late note that Part 2 may not be needed at all. Whatever the session rules out gets DELETED from MPI-379, not parked. Order and reasoning in tasks/MPI-424/brief.md: 379 first because it may drop the thumb strip and the Detect button and auto-fire detection, which every card below inherits and which directly sets MPI-421's scope; then 421 (cache the dispatches, queue what survives); then 382 (finish the shared strip BEFORE new tools inherit it); then 368 (cheapest tool, pure geometry); then 375 (paint, introduces the RGBA layer); then 373 last, because its erase-to-reveal layer IS that paint layer. This card holds no implementation of its own.

Umbrella re-sequenced to FIVE cards after MPI-379 was rejected outright in the brainstorm this card scheduled. New order: MPI-382 (in doing, user picked it up) -> 421 -> 368 -> 375 -> 373. MPI-421 was second because 379 might have auto-fired detection; with the chip strip and Detect button staying it is independent and simpler. brief.md carries the rejection record so the reasoning is not lost with the card.

Brainstorm complete. Architecture agreed with the user and written into brief.md: three toolbar groups (Mask / Paint / Composite), a floating Detect strip, two shared engines each mounted twice, and composite as one operation with two front ends fed by pasted slots. Order is now MPI-425 (taxonomy) -> 382 (Adjust) -> 368 (gizmo) -> 375 (paint + brush engine + alpha brushes) -> 373 (composite), with 421 independent.
